Get OPTN/UNOS Region Boundaries

Source: R/unos_regions_function.R
get_hrsa_optn_regions.Rd

Returns OPTN/UNOS region boundaries from the package's internal state-level UNOS region spatial dataset.

Usage

get_hrsa_optn_regions(
  crs = 4326,
  noncontiguous = c("exclude", "shift", "include")
)

Arguments

crs

Coordinate reference system of the result: anything sf::st_crs() accepts, such as an EPSG code. The default, 4326 (longitude/latitude), matches the layers that get_hrsa_transplant_centers() and get_hrsa_opo_service_areas() download. 5070 keeps the NAD83 / Conus Albers equal-area projection of UNOS_regions_sf. The boundaries are generalized Census cartographic files, drawn for maps, so areas and distances computed from them are approximate; use detailed boundaries for measurement. With noncontiguous = "shift" the result is always in 5070.

noncontiguous

What to do with Alaska, Hawaii and Puerto Rico. "exclude" (the default) leaves them out, for maps of transplant centers. "shift" keeps them and moves them below the contiguous states for display; the moved coordinates are map positions, not locations. "include" keeps them at their real locations, as OPTN defines the regions. The default is a convention for center maps, not part of the OPTN definition.

Value

An sf object with one feature per OPTN/UNOS region, in crs (EPSG:5070 with noncontiguous = "shift").

Details

This function uses the package's internal UNOS_regions_sf object, which contains state-level geometries assigned to OPTN/UNOS regions. The function dissolves those state-level geometries into one feature per OPTN/UNOS region.

Unlike the HRSA ArcGIS REGION_CD and REGION_NM fields, which appear to represent 10 HRSA/HHS administrative regions, this function returns the 11 OPTN/UNOS regions.

The regions are dissolved in the projection of UNOS_regions_sf (NAD83 / Conus Albers, EPSG:5070) and then transformed to crs.

Region 6 includes Alaska and Hawaii, and Region 3 includes Puerto Rico. Alaska has no transplant center, and on a national map these areas stretch the extent far beyond the contiguous states, so by default they are left out. noncontiguous = "shift" keeps them and moves them below the contiguous states with shift_noncontiguous(), for national maps of residents or donors; noncontiguous = "include" keeps them at their real locations, for spatial joins.

The regions are built from whole states, but OPTN splits three: Northern Virginia is in Region 2, eastern Vermont in Region 1 and southern Ohio in Region 11. Here all of Virginia is in Region 11, all of Vermont in Region 9 and all of Ohio in Region 10.

See also

sf::st_make_valid(), dplyr::summarise(), get_hrsa_transplant_centers(), shift_noncontiguous()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
regions <- get_hrsa_optn_regions()

regions
sf::st_crs(regions)
plot(regions["Region"])

# Keep the Albers projection of UNOS_regions_sf, as the bundled maps use
regions_albers <- get_hrsa_optn_regions(crs = 5070)

# All regions, with Alaska, Hawaii and Puerto Rico moved for a national map
regions_shifted <- get_hrsa_optn_regions(noncontiguous = "shift")
} # }
